model_annotation: This line plot depicts the relationship between accuracy (ACC) and co-occurrence number in a dataset, showing how event recognition performance is affected by the frequency of event co-occurrence. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number, scaled logarithmically from 10 to 1000 occurrences, indicating the frequency of event co-occurrences. The y-axis measures the accuracy percentage (ACC) in increments of 5%, ranging from 0 to 65%. Six distinct lines represent different methods or algorithms labeled as "Base," "Finite Temporal," "Initiation-Completion Error (IKE)," "Modification-Event Duration (MEND)," "Memorization Error (MEM)," and "RusGMT." The "Base" and "Finite Temporal" lines start at approximately 50% accuracy for events with 10 occurrences and gradually increase to 65% accuracy for the 1000th occurrence. The "IKE," "MEND," and "MEM" lines show a similar trend, initiating at slightly lower accuracy but still increasing to 65%. The "MEND" line, however, remains consistently below the others, indicating a lower performance in accuracy across the data points. All lines show a general ascent, suggesting increased event recognition accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with "Base" and "Finite Temporal" methods outperforming others across the board.
